=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:2094-2115 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: When a wait times out while the fix-up is still open, the branch sets `wait_ended_at="${now}"` but writes the `<!-- ai:unblock-wait-ended:v1 at=... -->` line only when the fix-up is already closed (lines 2100-2111). On the next run, the done-wait read-back (lines 1864-1877) finds no recorded end and falls back to the wait comment's later `updated_at`, which is the patch time.
  WHY: `now` is captured at line 1734, before the comments are fetched at line 1757. A "Planning blocked" comment posted after that fetch but before the wait-comment patch (line 2113) is not seen by this run. On the next run the strict `$block.at > $after` guard (line 619, called at line 2253) rejects that block, so the item goes to the model verdict instead of the #9518 close, which brings back the #9215 escalation. All three reviewers rated this MAJOR, with confidence 3, 4 and 3. Suggested fix: write the marker in this branch every time, using the final `wait_ended_at` (`at=${now}`). Disagreement: anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 explicitly rejected this finding. It says that keeping such a block with the judge is the intended behavior and that the PR's block_during_timed_out_wait test case asserts exactly that. minimax_minimax-m3 also notes this trade-off.

- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:lines 2098-2112 (write), 1866-1877 (read-back), 619 (guard), 2253 (call site), 1734 and 1757 (now vs. comment fetch) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The timed-out-wait branch sets `wait_ended_at="${now}"` but writes the `<!-- ai:unblock-wait-ended:v1 at=... -->` line only when the fix-up is already closed. If the fix-up is still open, the next run takes the wait end from the wait comment's later `updated_at` (line 1866).
  WHY: A block posted between the comment fetch (line 1757) and the wait-comment patch (line 2113) is not seen by this run. The next run then rejects it under the `$block.at > $after` guard (line 619) and sends the item to the model verdict, which is the #9215 symptom. Whether a block closes depends on timing. Suggested fix: record `at=${now}` and leave the guard as it is. The reviewer notes the trade-off that keeping such a block with the judge could also be read as intended behavior.
- HARDENING scripts/unblock_judge.sh:line 2253, `"${wait:+${wait_ended_at:-${wait_updated:-}}}"` | HARDENING_RISK_SCORE=2
  PROBLEM: If both `wait_ended_at` and `wait_updated` are empty, `block_after` is empty, which turns off the age guard at line 619 (`$after == ""`).
  WHY: A block of any age would then close the issue. Suggested fix: fall back to `wait_at` (`"${wait:+${wait_ended_at:-${wait_updated:-${wait_at:-}}}}"`) or skip the close. Estimated 1 line changed.
- HARDENING scripts/unblock_judge.sh:lines 611-620 and 629 (`marker_since="${block_at}"`) | HARDENING_RISK_SCORE=1
  PROBLEM: If `block_at` is empty, `marker_since` is empty and the `fixup=none` marker dedup at lines 631-632 loses its age check.
  WHY: A stale marker from an earlier block would suppress the new close comment. Suggested fix: return 1 when `block_at` is not a timestamp. Estimated 2 lines changed.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
